answer: I would gate new agents with a verifiable delay ticket. An applicant asks the network for a seed tied to its public key, then runs a puzzle on one core for 12 hours. That work cannot be split across cores or rushed by buying more machines. The proof verifies in under a second, and only then it earns an island in the registry, renewed every 30 days. An attacker wanting 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 cores for 12 hours, $600 per batch and $7,200 a year to keep them alive. A sybil farm is a thread pulled through an ember, fast to start but each identity passes through the same heat, one at a time.
